newsitem.title: POLAND: ZLOTY CLOSES STRONGER, NBP-BILL SALE BOOSTS DEPOS.
newsitem.headline: ZLOTY CLOSES STRONGER, NBP-BILL SALE BOOSTS DEPOS.

text.p: The Polish zloty closed slightly firmer against the parity rate after trading flat for most of the day thanks to a strong opening on the back of the dollar's weakness, dealers said.

They said banks had no curreny buying interest because of the central bank's statements that it could soon raise official interest rates and because of recent rises in yields of NBP-bills offered to money market dealers.
"Banks see that market rates are rising and there is no interest to buy currencies as everybody is waiting for official rates to move as well," said Piotr Nowak from BPH SA.

The zloty closed at 3.18/3.15 pct from the trading band centre, barely changed from opening but stronger than Monday's 3.13/3.09 pct. It closed at 2.8770/80 to the dollar, up from 2.8805/15 on Monday and at 1.8415/20 to the mark, down from 1.8392/02.

The central bank sold 600 million of 182-day NBP-bills at an average yield 0.01 point up at 22.00 percent and 33 million zlotys of 273-day NBP-bills against a 300 million offer at an average rate 1.04 point up at 21.01 percent.
"The central bank probably wants to establish a positive NBP-bill yield curve, and bids for 273-day paper must have been too high," said a dealer at a foreign bank here.
Dealers expected the central bank to rise the 273-day bill yield to some 22.20 percent because nine month deposits rose to around 21.75/22.80 percent before the auction.

Dealers said the NBP-bill yield rise could be capped by a slower rise in T-bill yields and a growing spread between the two instruments. Nine-month T-bills were quoted at 20.20-25/19.80 percent in secondary trade.
O/N deposit rates were 0.1 point up at 21.80/22.20 percent.
Tomorrow/next were at 21.85/22.20 percent against the opening's 21.85/22.15 percent after the NBP drained PLN 394 million zlotys for 14 days at a flat maximum rate of 21.64 percent.
